branch_005.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Enable customers to browse products and place orders' is semantically identical to the existing High-Level Goal 'Discover and order local produce' (which describes the same intention: browsing offers and placing orders). The project description supports this intention, but since another HLG for the same actor already covers this functional intention, keeping both would result in redundant goals that merely split one stakeholder intention into wording variants. Therefore, the original goal should be removed to avoid duplication.

branch_007.rationale: The project description explicitly states that 'Once payment has been successfully completed, customers can reserve a time slot for collecting their products from the store.' It also mentions that if a customer fails to collect at the scheduled time, reminders are sent, implying the existence of a schedule that can be viewed or managed. The original High-Level Goal 'Enable customers to manage product collection time slots' accurately captures this functional intention. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Customer Product Collection Time Slots' aligns with this. There is no other High-Level Goal for the Customer actor that covers this specific aspect of pickup logistics (other Customer HLGs cover ordering, payment, and fair-play scores). The scope is appropriate and supported by the documentation. The parent High-Level Goal (HLG) explicitly requires customers to be able to 'book, view, cancel, and modify' their reserved time slots. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) cover all four of these capabilities: llg_001 (reserve/book), llg_002 (retrieve/view), llg_003 (cancel), and llg_004 (modify). The documentation supports these actions as part of the customer's post-payment workflow. There are no contradictions with the documentation, and no essential capabilities explicitly required by the parent HLG are missing. The sibling HLGs regarding store employee logistics do not conflict with these customer-facing management goals.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: The project description outlines a weekly purchasing cycle involving farmers, customers, and store employees. The current High-Level Goals (HLGs) comprehensively cover the functional intentions of all identified actors: Farmers (providing availability, confirming quantities, delivering goods), Customers (browsing/ordering, managing payments/wallets, scheduling pickups, maintaining fair-play scores), and Store Employees (managing orders, handling payments, coordinating pickups, verifying deliveries). Specific workflow steps such as order modification due to availability, automatic payment execution, SMS/email notifications, and fair-play score calculation are covered by the broader stakeholder intentions already listed (e.g., 'Manage personal payment for purchases', 'Maintain a reliable purchasing record', 'Support customer order management'). There are no distinct, documented functional intentions for new actors or existing actors that are absent from the current HLG list.
